From 7e57523490cd2efb52b1ea97f2e0a74c0fb634cd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:38:58 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] netfs: Fix read abandonment during retry

Under certain circumstances, all the remaining subrequests from a read
request will get abandoned during retry.  The abandonment process expects
the 'subreq' variable to be set to the place to start abandonment from, but
it doesn't always have a useful value (it will be uninitialised on the
first pass through the loop and it may point to a deleted subrequest on
later passes).

Fix the first jump to "abandon:" to set subreq to the start of the first
subrequest expected to need retry (which, in this abandonment case, turned
out unexpectedly to no longer have NEED_RETRY set).

Also clear the subreq pointer after discarding superfluous retryable
subrequests to cause an oops if we do try to access it.

Fixes: ee4cdf7ba857 ("netfs: Speed up buffered reading")
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/3775287.1773848338@warthog.procyon.org.uk
Reviewed-by: Paulo Alcantara (Red Hat) <pc@manguebit.org>
cc: Paulo Alcantara <pc@manguebit.org>
cc: netfs@lists.linux.dev
cc: linux-fsdevel@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/netfs/read_retry.c b/fs/netfs/read_retry.c
index 7793ba5e3e8f..cca9ac43c077 100644
--- a/fs/netfs/read_retry.c
+++ b/fs/netfs/read_retry.c
@@ -93,8 +93,10 @@ static void netfs_retry_read_subrequests(struct netfs_io_request *rreq)
 		       from->start, from->transferred, from->len);
 
 		if (test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_FAILED, &from->flags) ||
-		    !test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_NEED_RETRY, &from->flags))
+		    !test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_NEED_RETRY, &from->flags)) {
+			subreq = from;
 			goto abandon;
+		}
 
 		list_for_each_continue(next, &stream->subrequests) {
 			subreq = list_entry(next, struct netfs_io_subrequest, rreq_link);
@@ -178,6 +180,7 @@ static void netfs_retry_read_subrequests(struct netfs_io_request *rreq)
 				if (subreq == to)
 					break;
 			}
+			subreq = NULL;
 			continue;
 		}
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies `fs/netfs/read_retry.c` to fix a bug where all remaining subrequests in a read request could be incorrectly abandoned during retry due to an improperly maintained `subreq` pointer.

**Modifications in `fs/netfs/read_retry.c`:**

1. **When abandoning a subrequest** (line 96):  
   Before jumping to the `abandon` label, the code now explicitly sets `subreq = from`. This ensures that abandonment starts from the correct subrequest, rather than using an uninitialized or stale pointer (e.g., pointing to a previously deleted subrequest).

2. **After discarding superfluous retryable subrequests** (line 183):  
   After the inner loop that removes subrequests between `from` and `to`, the pointer `subreq` is set to `NULL`. This prevents accidental later access to a subrequest that has been freed, causing a potential use-after-free or oops if accessed.

**Relationship between modifications:**  
Both changes ensure the `subreq` variable always holds a valid (or safely null) pointer at critical points in the retry logic. The first fix corrects the start point for abandonment, while the second clears the pointer after deletion, together preventing incorrect abandonment and dangling pointer dereferences. This resolves the read abandonment issue described in the commit message.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_FAILED, &from->flags) ||
    !test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_NEED_RETRY, &from->flags))
    goto abandon;
```
and the missing `subreq = NULL;` after the superfluous removal loop (i.e., after the `list_for_each_entry_safe_from` block that deletes subrequests).

Reason:
When the condition is true, the code jumps to the `abandon` label without setting `subreq`. On the first loop iteration, `subreq` is uninitialized (stack variable); on later iterations, it may point to a previously deleted subrequest. The `abandon` label starts its loop from `subreq`, so an uninitialized or dangling pointer causes the loop to start at an unpredictable or invalid location, leading to all remaining subrequests being incorrectly abandoned. Additionally, after discarding superfluous subrequests, `subreq` is left pointing to a deleted object, which can cause a use-after-free if later code touches it.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_FAILED, &from->flags) ||
    !test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_NEED_RETRY, &from->flags)) {
    subreq = from;
    goto abandon;
}
```
and after the superfluous removal loop:
```c
subreq = NULL;
```

Reason:
By setting `subreq = from;` before the `goto abandon`, the abandonment loop now starts from the current subrequest `from`, which ensures that the correct range of subrequests is processed. The `subreq = NULL;` after removing superfluous subrequests clears the pointer so that any subsequent use of `subreq` will cause an explicit NULL-pointer dereference (oops) rather than a silent use-after-free, making the code safer and easier to debug.
